channel.title: Launchpad Digital
channel.description: Florida news, briefs and getaways from Launchpad Digital, reported from primary sources.

item.title: Federal Public Assistance Approved for 15 Panhandle and Big Bend Counties Hit by Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The money helps local governments and some nonprofits pay for debris removal and repairs. Help for individual households is still under federal review.

item.title: Jacksonville Sheriff's Office Releases Video and Details of Oct. 11 Police Shooting on Mar Vic Lane
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: JSO says officers shot and killed a 34-year-old woman after she fired at them. The State Attorney's Office will review the shooting, and JSO says its conclusions are still pending.

item.title: South Florida's East Coast Faces More Coastal Flooding Through the Week; Rip Current Risk Stays High
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: The National Weather Service in Miami says high tides could bring moderate flooding through at least Thursday evening, with hazardous beach and boating conditions through Thursday.

item.title: Federal Reserve Holds Key Interest Rate at 3.75% to 4%; Two Policymakers Wanted a Hike
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The Fed's rate committee voted 10 to 2 to leave the federal funds rate unchanged. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented, saying they'd have raised it a quarter point. Chairman Kevin Warsh also announced a change to the committee's meeting schedule starting in 2027.

item.title: FHP Trooper Seriously Injured After Pickup Hits His Patrol Car in SR 429 Work Zone Near Bay Lake
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: The trooper was airlifted to a hospital and is in stable condition. FHP says the truck's driver failed to move over for the patrol car's emergency lights, and charges are pending.

item.title: DeSantis Awards $100 Million for 45 Springs and Water Supply Projects Across Florida
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Half the money goes to 23 springs restoration projects and half to 22 alternative water supply projects, including $10 million for Tampa Bay Water and $12.6 million for seven Polk County communities.

item.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions 10 People and a Russia-Based Center Over North Korean IT Worker Schemes
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: Treasury says North Korean tech workers use fake identities to get hired by U.S. companies, and the regime keeps most of their pay to fund its weapons programs.

item.title: Panthers Score Three Power-Play Goals in 5-1 Win at Winnipeg
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: Carter Verhaeghe scored twice, Matthew Tkachuk had four assists and Brady Tkachuk added a goal and two assists. The two teams meet again Friday in Sunrise.

item.title: U.K. Announces £10 Billion in New Support for Ukraine, Its Largest Package Yet
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The British government says the money includes £500 million for Ukraine's air defenses this winter. It was announced alongside the U.K.'s 2026 Budget.

item.title: Florida Agencies Thank the People Behind the Badge on National First Responders Day
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: Police and sheriff's offices from Orlando to Tampa used Oct. 28 to recognize officers, deputies, dispatchers and the newest 911 call-takers.

item.title: More Than 3.5 Million Floridians Have Now Voted in the Nov. 3 General Election
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Nearly 370,000 more ballots were cast in a single day, the state's figures show. Early votes now top 1.9 million, and about 847,000 mail ballots are still out six days before Election Day.

item.title: Midday Brief: Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since the Morning Brief come first, then this morning's stories, with any verified updates marked.

item.title: Florida AG Charges Kissimmee Man With 100 Felony Counts of Child Sexual Abuse Material, Sues AI Platform A2E
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: Attorney General James Uthmeier says the company behind A2E lets users make sexualized images of real Floridians, including children. He wants a court to stop it.

item.title: AG Uthmeier Says His Office Is Launching an Investigation Into a 'CCP-Controlled Corporation' Operating in Florida
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: The attorney general's post quoted a video about yacht maker Ferretti Group and its Fort Lauderdale property. Here's what the official records show and what Florida law says.

item.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and a Rwandan Bank Over Support for M23 Rebels
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: Treasury says Rwanda's defense ministry directed troops fighting alongside the M23 armed group in eastern Congo, and that the Zigama Credit and Savings Society moved money and gold for them.

item.title: Weeki Wachee Springs: the mermaid show and a first-magnitude spring
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: A classic Old Florida attraction in Hernando County, where mermaids perform in water that flows from a first-magnitude spring.

item.title: Apalachicola: two small state museums in an old Gulf cotton port
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: A Franklin County fishing town on the Forgotten Coast, with an 1838 cotton merchant's home and a museum to the doctor who patented mechanical refrigeration.

item.title: India Sends Federal Team to Investigate a Cheetah's Death From Pellet Injuries
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: The 19-month-old male was born in India to a cheetah brought in under Project Cheetah, the country's effort to reintroduce the big cats.

item.title: A Horse Rider's Sharp Eyes Help New Zealand Remove 141 Invasive Plants From Ninety Mile Beach
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: New Zealand's Department of Conservation says one beachgoer's photos and phone call led crews to a hidden patch of sea spurge before it could spread.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Nears 10,000 Confirmed Cases as Kenya and Nigeria Report Imported Cases
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: European and World Health Organization health officials say the risk to travelers remains low, and WHO advises against travel or trade restrictions.

item.title: Five European Defense Ministers Pledge a Bigger Role for Europe Within NATO
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: The defense ministers of France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom said the U.S. "is and will remain an indispensable Ally" and reaffirmed support for Ukraine.

item.title: India and Mexico Formally Launch Talks on a Preferential Trade Agreement
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The two governments signed terms of reference that set the scope and roadmap for negotiations, India's Commerce Ministry says.

item.title: Trick-or-Treating Saturday? Orange County Sheriff's Office Shares Its Halloween Safety Tips
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Go in a group, stay on well-lit streets, cross at corners and check the candy, the agency says.

item.title: Jacksonville Sheriff's Office Shows How Its Vice Detectives and Animal Care Officers Rescue Neglected Dogs
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: A new video from the agency follows emergency warrants in animal cruelty cases and the dogs taken to safety. The Sheriff's Office asks anyone who suspects cruelty to call 904-630-0500.

item.title: Sarasota County Residents Turn In More Than 46 Pounds of Unwanted Medication at Sheriff's Office Take Back Event
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: The Sheriff's Office thanked the community for taking part in the DEA Drug Take Back event over the weekend.

item.title: Israel Counts Votes After Election; Partial Counts Show Neither Bloc at a 61-Seat Majority
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The counts below are partial and unofficial, as reported by news outlets. Final results will come from Israel's Central Elections Committee once all ballots, including soldiers' absentee votes, are counted.

item.title: Coastal Flood Warnings Extended Into Friday on Much of Florida's Atlantic Coast; Keys Remain Under Major Flooding Warning
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The National Weather Service says flooding around high tide, rough surf and dangerous rip currents will continue for days from Nassau County to the Treasure Coast. South Florida's warning ends tonight, and an advisory follows.

item.title: Three Proposed Constitutional Amendments Are on Florida's Nov. 3 Ballot: What Each One Would Do, in the State's Own Words
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: All three were placed on the ballot by the Legislature. They cover the state's budget stabilization fund, a tax exemption for farm equipment, and a larger homestead exemption. Each needs at least 60% of the vote to pass.

item.title: Morning Brief: Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since the Evening Brief come first, then earlier stories that are still developing.

item.title: Myakka River State Park: Florida's first wild and scenic river
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: Fifty-eight square miles of wetlands, prairie and pinelands east of Sarasota, along the state's first designated wild and scenic river.

item.title: Paynes Prairie: wild bison and horses south of Gainesville
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: Florida's first state preserve, next to the small town of Micanopy, is the only place in the state where visitors can see wild-roaming bison and horses.

item.title: Cedar Key: a small Gulf island town and its history museum
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: An island town on Florida's Nature Coast, with a state park museum, salt marshes and a historic waterfront.

item.title: Ichetucknee Springs: a quiet spring run near Fort White
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: Eight major springs feed the 6-mile Ichetucknee River in a North Central Florida state park best known for tubing and paddling.

item.title: Hontoon Island: a ferry-only state park on the St. Johns River
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: An island park west of DeLand reached only by private boat or the free park ferry, with trails, a visitor center and thousands of years of history.

item.title: Jonathan Dickinson State Park: Hobe Mountain and the wild Loxahatchee
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: The largest state park in Southeast Florida, in Hobe Sound, mixes an ancient sand dune, a wild and scenic river and a 1930s pioneer homestead.

item.title: At Least 64 Dead After Two High-Speed Trains Collide Near Urda, Spain
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: Officials confirm 64 dead and 58 injured, including a Guardia Civil officer. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has visited the site and says officials are working to find the cause.

item.title: Man Charged With Murder in Taliaferro Avenue Shooting in Tampa, Sheriff's Office Says
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: Hillsborough County detectives arrested Nathan Campbell, 26, in Gibsonton less than a day after Ronnie Sheppard, 29, was shot and killed late Tuesday night.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias Recovery Centers in the Panhandle Begin Closing; Santa Rosa Site's Last Day Is Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Multi-Agency Resource Centers in Santa Rosa, Washington, Walton and Escambia counties have set closing dates this week. Here is where they are and what to bring.

item.title: Hillsborough Sheriff's Office Celebrates Its 2026 Class of Volunteer Citizen Patrol Graduates
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: The new volunteers trained in crime prevention and first aid and will serve as "an extra set of eyes and ears," the agency said.

item.title: Who's Running Statewide in Florida on Nov. 3: The Qualified Candidates, From the State's Own List
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: The Division of Elections lists qualified candidates for U.S. Senate, governor, attorney general, chief financial officer and agriculture commissioner. Here they are, in the order the state lists them.

item.title: Evening Brief: Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since the Afternoon Brief come first, then earlier stories that are still developing.

item.title: Trump Announces EPA Proposal to Revise Biden-Era Methane Rules for Oil and Gas Wells
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The EPA says the proposal would save $45 billion in costs and add an estimated 210 million barrels of oil. It is a proposal, not a final rule, and the public will get at least 45 days to comment.

item.title: First Venezuelan Oil Cargo Under U.S. Deal Arrives in Corpus Christi as Trump and Rubio Visit the Port
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The White House says the 1 million barrels will be refined in Texas. The producer says it delivered the first cargo at no cost to taxpayers under an August agreement with the Departments of State and War.

item.title: Trump Rallies in Corinth, Mississippi, for Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, Urges Early Voting
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Speaking eight days before the Nov. 3 midterm election, the president asked supporters to vote and said he was heading to Texas next. The GOP's official channel lists rallies in Corpus Christi and Lubbock on Tuesday.

item.title: More Than 3.1 Million Floridians Have Already Voted in the Nov. 3 General Election
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: State figures compiled Tuesday morning show about 1.66 million early votes and 1.49 million mail ballots returned, with nearly 1 million mail ballots still out. Here is the count by party and what voters still need to know.

item.title: Afternoon Brief: Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since the Midday Brief come first, then earlier stories that are still developing.

item.title: Localized Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Takes Effect in Oleshky So Aid Can Reach Trapped Residents
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The White House says First Lady Melania Trump brokered the truce in the Russian-occupied city. She said Tuesday it began two days early and now covers a wider area of the Kherson region.

item.title: Two Boaters Brought Safely to Shore After Sailboat Capsizes Near Tampa's Ballast Point Pier
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office deputies righted the 16-foot sailboat and towed it in. The agency's reminder for anyone heading out: wear a life jacket.

item.title: Federal Survey: Rate of Serious Violent Victimization Fell 25% in 2025, Preliminary Estimates Show
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The Bureau of Justice Statistics' first full-year numbers from its redesigned crime survey also show property victimization down 19%. The estimates are preliminary and may change.

item.title: U.S. Consumer Confidence Rises 7.5 Points in October as Gas Prices Ease, Conference Board Says
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: The index rose to 91.7 from 84.2 in September. The group's economist said confidence is still on a long-term downward trend, and consumers planned less spending on services and durable goods.
